proposal.title: Use Blosc byte-shuffle for float32 chunk compression
proposal.hypothesis: Operational evidence shows Zarr metadata is 0.0% of measured output bytes and chunk payloads account for essentially all 109455072 output bytes, so footprint changes must target data-chunk encoding rather than metadata or provider/cache behavior. If the existing lossless Blosc+Zstd compressor uses byte-shuffle instead of bitshuffle for the published float32 ERA5 fields, stable high-order float bytes across smooth spatial grids may form longer byte runs for Zstd than bit-plane rearrangement of noisy mantissa bits, reducing output_bytes while preserving all frozen array paths, dimensions, coordinates, selector paths, Zarr v3 consolidated publication, validation, and semantic values.
proposal.expected_tradeoffs: Materialization_seconds may change slightly because byte-shuffle has different preconditioning cost and compressed payload size. Consumer_samples_per_second may be neutral or move modestly depending on decompression speed, but the experiment targets only output_bytes.

edits.rationale: Switches only the lossless Blosc preconditioner for data chunks, keeping the same compressor family, level, chunk layout, dtype handling, validation, and public store interface while testing a distinct footprint mechanism.

proposal.validation_plan: Run the evaluator unchanged and compare the multi-objective vector, with acceptance focused on lower output_bytes. Confirm contract correctness, semantic equivalence, provenance/security, rerun safety, frozen channel mappings, coordinate paths, consolidated Zarr v3 output, and validation still pass.
